stories.primary_headline: 'Step into the Light': Juhi Chawla makes surprise cameo in latest 'Shot on iPhone 18 Pro' ad ahead of Diwali

primary_source.headline: 'Step into the Light': Juhi Chawla makes surprise cameo in latest 'Shot on iPhone 18 Pro' ad ahead of Diwali
primary_source.content: For years, Apple has been a master at marketing its products, especially with the Shot on iPhone feature ads. It has good knack of finding the art directors who are capable of capturing the local cultural aspects and also flawlessly highlight the photography capabilities of the new iPhones.With soaring demand for iPhone 18 Pro models worldwide, Apple has released fun, catchy ad- 'Step into the Light' with popular music track-- Roop Suhana Lagta Hai- composed by Anu Malik in the 1994 film 'The Gentleman', starring legendary Telugu star Chiranjeevi and Bollywood icon Juhi Chawla ahead of Diwali (aka Deepavali).Apple Watch saves senior doctor: Timely alert helps him get heart valve surgery done in the nick of timeDirected by Sanjay Garg (Raw Mango founder), the new 'Shot on iPhone' ad features ptures how India looks during the festival of light. The video was filmed at Tijara Fort, a restored 19th-century royal palace in Rajasthan.The film’s concept revolves around stepping out of darkness into light through dance. Also, it brings together a diverse cast from across India, each wearing Raw Mango looks with details specific to their region.The icing on the cake is the surprise cameo by the OG Juhi Chawla, the lead female protagonist from the movie 'The Gentleman'.Juhi Chawla on Shot on iPhone 18 Pro ad.“Diwali, for me, is the biggest festival of the year. It represents a change in weather where we welcome winter in the company of people we love,” said Sanjay Garg.Behind-the-scene: Apple's shot on iPhone 18 Pro ad (screen-grab)With light at the centre of the Diwali festival, the film, as you can see in the video (below), was shot in low light to showcase the most advanced cameras of the iPhone 18 Pro series.The biggest upgrade we see in the iPhone 18 Pro is the dynamic variable aperture. Apple achieved this feat by incorporating six laser-cut blades, which can smoothly transition between different apertures, making it incredibly simple to capture the best shot by automatically adjusting for depth of field and lighting.Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max Review: Powerful performer with exceptionally good cameraCombined with a new sensor that improves image quality, the result is better low-light photography, crisper detail in the back of group photos, and more unique shots.Also, the variable aperture offers more control for creative filmmakers to manually adjust any of the four aperture settings in the native camera app.Tips & Tricks: Master Deepavali photography on the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone DuoGet the latest news on new launches, gadget reviews, apps, cybersecurity, and more on personal technology only on DH Tech.

brief_bullets: James Gates has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging that ChatGPT facilitated his wife Cheryl Gates’s attempt to poison him. According to the complaint, Cheryl utilized the AI to generate lethal dosage instructions and concealment strategies for oleander poisoning, framing her queries as self-defense. Despite the suspicious nature of these requests, the lawsuit claims OpenAI failed to implement necessary safety guardrails to terminate the interaction. Cheryl Gates has since been indicted by a grand jury on charges of attempted first-degree murder and food contamination. This case highlights critical concerns regarding the liability of AI developers when their platforms are weaponized to execute criminal acts, challenging existing protections for generative AI providers under current legal frameworks.

brief_bullets: Tech giants Meta, Google, and TikTok have filed lawsuits against California Attorney General Rob Bonta to block AB 1709, a state law aimed at curbing addictive social media features for users under 16. The legislation mandates the removal of personalized feeds and autoplay functions, threatening fines of up to $50,000 per violation. Plaintiffs argue the law violates First Amendment free speech protections by interfering with editorial content curation and conflicts with federal Section 230 immunity. Additionally, privacy advocates warn that the compliance requirements could force platforms to collect excessive user data, potentially undermining anonymity. This legal confrontation sets a critical precedent for state-level digital regulation versus federal protections, testing the boundaries of corporate liability regarding minor safety and algorithmic design.
why_it_matters_bullets: This litigation will define the legal limits of state authority to regulate algorithmic content delivery and minor safety online.

stories.primary_headline: IISc honours eight alumni for contributions to science, technology and society

primary_source.headline: IISc honours eight alumni for contributions to science, technology and society
primary_source.content: Bengaluru:&nbsp;This year, the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) honours eight scientists and engineers with its Distinguished Alumnus/Alumna Awards and Young Alumnus/Alumna Medals.The awards recognise alumni/ae who have made exceptional contributions to their professions, to society, and to the Institute. Each nomination is assessed by a committee under the oversight of the Director, IISc.This year's Distinguished Alumnus/Alumna awardees are B S Manjunath, Dipakar Das Sarma, Jagannath Nayak, Maruthi R Akella, and Rajat Moona. The Young Alumnus/Alumna Medals, given to researchers under the age of 40, are conferred on Abhishek Sinha, Geethu Joseph, and Himanshu Joshi.The awardees will be honoured at a ceremony to be held on 19 December 2026, at the JN Tata Auditorium, IISc.Distinguished Alumnus/Alumna Awardees1. B S Manjunath is a globally recognised computer scientist and academic leader, and the Frank Koenig Distinguished Chair in Signals and Systems and Distinguished Professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara, USA. His work spans computer vision, content-based image retrieval, and biological image informatics, including BisQue, an open-source platform for scientific image management adopted as a core service of NSF CyVerse. He contributed foundational video descriptors to the MPEG-7 standard, co-founded the company Mayachitra, and has supervised 53 PhD graduates.B S Manjunath i 2. Dipankar Das Sarma is an internationally renowned condensed matter physicist and materials chemist, currently the ANRF National Science Chair and Emeritus Professor at the Solid State and Structural Chemistry Unit, IISc. His work includes the discovery of the covalent-insulator state, kinetic energy-driven ferromagnetism in Sr2FeMoO6, and depth-sensitive photoemission techniques for probing nanocrystals and buried interfaces. He also spearheaded India's access to international synchrotron facilities, establishing Indo-Italian beamlines at Elettra.&nbsp;Dipankar Das SarmaCentralised street light monitoring system promises better public lighting in Bengaluru 3. Jagannath Nayak is a distinguished defence scientist and Director General of Missiles and Strategic Systems at DRDO. His career spans photonics, fibre lasers, and inertial navigation. He led the indigenous development of high-accuracy Fibre Optic Gyroscopes for programmes such as Akash, Nag, and Astra, and the creation of India's first operational Laser Directed Energy Weapon system. His work has led to complete indigenisation of critical avionics and laser systems.&nbsp;Jagannath Nayak 3. Maruthi R Akella is a globally renowned aerospace scientist and control systems engineer, who currently holds the Cockrell Family Chair in Engineering at The University of Texas at Austin, USA. His research covers spacecraft attitude estimation, adaptive control, vision-guided robotics, and orbital mechanics. His algorithms provided onboard guidance for Intuitive Machines' IM-1 lunar lander mission, the first US moon landing in over 50 years.&nbsp;Maruthi R Akella 4. Rajat Moona is an internationally renowned computer scientist and technologist, and Director of IIT Gandhinagar. His work has shaped India's digital infrastructure, from the Smart Card OS Template Architecture (SCOSTA) behind driving licences and e-passports to India's Electronic Toll Collection system and FASTag. He architected the M3 Electronic Voting Machine, VVPAT, and the National Voters' Service Portal, and as Director General of C-DAC, advanced national supercomputing through PARAM Yuva II.&nbsp;Rajat Moona Young Alumnus/Alumna Medallists1. Abhishek Sinha is a leading theoretical computer scientist, currently a Reader at the School of Technology and Computer Science, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Mumbai. He has resolved long-standing open problems in online learning and network optimisation, including a framework that achieves optimal learning and long-term constraint satisfaction simultaneously. His work has appeared in venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, and IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking.&nbsp;Abhishek Sinha 2. Geethu Joseph is a tenured Assistant Professor at Delft University of Technology, Netherlands. Her work introduces frameworks for resource-aware control systems and sensing methods for autonomous driving, radar, and wireless communications, with industrial partners including NXP, ASML, imec, and TNO. She is an Associate Editor of the IEEE Sensors Journal.&nbsp;Geethu Joseph 3. Himanshu Joshi a researcher in computational biophysics, multiscale molecular simulations, DNA nanotechnology, and an Assistant Professor of Biotechnology at IIT Hyderabad. His work spans aquaporins, ion channels, nanopore sequencing, and water desalination, including artificial water channels for ultrafast water transport and DNA origami-based ion channels.Himanshu Joshi

The awards recognise alumni/ae who have made exceptional contributions to their professions, to society, and to the Institute.

stories.primary_headline: Steps being taken to curb man-animal conflict in Bandipur: Minister Ramalinga Reddy

primary_source.headline: Steps being taken to curb man-animal conflict in Bandipur: Minister Ramalinga Reddy
primary_source.content: Gundlupet: Minister of Forest, Ecology and Environment Ramalinga Reddy assured that necessary measures are being taken to prevent man-animal conflict in Bandipur forest area.Speaking to media persons, here on Friday, he said, "There is no delay in the probe related to the shootout incident by the Forest department in Hanur, which claimed three lives. The CoD is investigating and we will not intervene. The anti-poaching camps and quarters that were destroyed by mob after the incident are being repaired. The department personnel need not fear and should perform their duties. Besides, there is no permission to possess rifles without licenses. Those possessing the same should surrender to the government, or face legal action."Necessary steps would be taken for the establishing Kaniyanapura elephant corridor of Bandipur Tiger Reserve. Private land if any, would be acquired for the project, he said.Tribal woman killed in tiger attack near Bandipur Reserve in MysuruDiscussions have been held with the State Wildlife Board on announcing M M Hills as Tiger reserve, but locals are against it. The government will take a final decision soon, he said. On illegal resorts and homestays at eco-sensitive zones at Bandipur, he said, permission is given only to resorts that have licenses. Notices are served to those operating without licenses. Some have stay orders from the court. The supervisory committee will monitor this. Reddy held a meeting with the Forest Department officials on the human-animal conflict in the region and gathered information.Principal Chief Conservator of Forest (PCCF) Kumar Pushkar said, "34 people have died due to wild animal attacks in Chamarajanagar district in the last 11 months, and tops the district. Kodagu is in second place. Thirty one tigers have been safely rescued in the last one year."The railway barricades have been useful and the government should grant funds for erecting barricades for 73-kms, he appealed to the minister.Bandipur Conservator of Forest Nandish said, "There are 13 ranges in Bandipur, covering around 1,036 kms. In all, 136 villages come under the forest area. Totally 314 personnel are on duty, with 213 watchers on outsourced basis."Artificial Intelligence cameras and drones are being used to monitor the movement of the wild animals. With this, we get information on the movement of elephants and wild animals near the villages and help to alert the villagers, he said.Reddy said that out of 13 ranges in Bandipur, only four ranges have no man-animal conflict. "Around 38% of the forest is covered with lantana. The biodiversity will be affected if machines are used for clearing it and the forest will be affected if left unattended. Hence, measures would be taken to clear them without affecting the forest," he said.MLA M Ganesh Prasad, APCCF Manoj Ranjan, CCF Malathi Priaya, Ravishankar CF, Mysuru Circle, ACF Paramesh, Vinod were present.

stories.primary_headline: Technology must be guided by character, commitment and compassion: PGIMER Director

primary_source.headline: Technology must be guided by character, commitment and compassion: PGIMER Director
primary_source.content: Mangaluru:&nbsp;Technology and digital advancements must be guided by character, commitment and compassion to ensure their meaningful use for the welfare of society, said Prof Vivek Lal, Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh.Addressing 16th convocation of Nitte Deemed to be University at Deraakatte, he urged students to draw inspiration from Swami Vivekananda's ideals and uphold the values of character, commitment and compassion, which he described as the three essential pillars for the younger generation."Technology and digital assets have no meaning if there is no island of commitment, compassion and character to harness them," he said, emphasising that India had immense technological capabilities as well as the trust and faith of its patients.Mangaluru woman attacked with iron rod in car; man arrested for attempted murder Highlighting the importance of patient-centred healthcare, he said the biggest asset of the country was not technology but the faith patients placed in healthcare professionals. He urged medical graduates to remain grateful to patients and dedicate their knowledge and skills to reduce human suffering.Referring to Swami Vivekananda's historic address at the Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893, Prof Lal said the spiritual leader's teachings on character and social responsibility remained relevant even today. He called upon graduates to give back to society in whatever way possible and make service an integral part of their professional lives.He also cautioned students against becoming overconfident about their digital knowledge in the age of artificial intelligence. While acknowledging AI as an extraordinary technological advancement, he stressed the need to ensure that technology was used responsibly and did not become a threat to humanity.Drawing a parallel with the destructive consequences of nuclear technology, he said humanity must ensure that artificial intelligence was not misused. He urged students to follow the ideals of Swami Vivekananda rather than blindly placing their faith in technology.Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, he said the country could achieve the goal even earlier if the younger generation developed an enlightened mindset and worked with a sense of responsibility.Referring to India's rich medical heritage, he recalled the contributions of Sushruta, regarded as the father of surgery, and Charaka, regarded as the father of medicine. He said their prime focus was healing and relieving the suffering of patients.Nitte DU Chancellor N Vishal Hegde presided over the gathering. Degrees were conferred on 1455 graduates.&nbsp;

stories.primary_headline: It's a weird time to buy a laptop, but the new MacBook Pro doesn't skimp on quality

primary_source.headline: It's a weird time to buy a laptop, but the new MacBook Pro doesn't skimp on quality
primary_source.content:
Apple's new MacBook Pro is expensive as hell.
Let's get that out there right away, because for a lot of people, it will be the only thing that matters. As with so many things in life, though, you get what you pay for. There's no questioning the quality of the laptop's display or most of its other hardware components.
But should you buy it? Well, that's a complicated question in 2026.Read full article
